questions.q: A young man was distressed by political news. What reminder did the author give him?
options: He should stop following the news
Not quite. The article says: History is in God’s hands, not any ruler’s; one should go on with one’s work and be friendly to all.
History is in God’s hands, not any ruler’s; one should go on with one’s work and be friendly to all
Yes. No political rule is permanent.
He should leave the country at once
Not quite. The article says: History is in God’s hands, not any ruler’s; one should go on with one’s work and be friendly to all.
He should join a protest movement
Not quite. The article says: History is in God’s hands, not any ruler’s; one should go on with one’s work and be friendly to all.
questions.rationale: “It is God who shapes human history, and not any political ruler. Muslims must always adopt the attitude of: Do your work, and be friendly in your behaviour towards others.”

questions.q: The article says a believer lives between hope and fear, sometimes certain and sometimes doubtful about himself. Why does it see value in this?
options: It shows his faith is weak
Not quite. The article says: The unease keeps his thinking alive, so that he goes on learning and growing.
It keeps him from sinning by frightening him
Not quite. The article says: The unease keeps his thinking alive, so that he goes on learning and growing.
The unease keeps his thinking alive, so that he goes on learning and growing
Right. Even the Companions felt it.
It makes him depend on scholars
Not quite. The article says: The unease keeps his thinking alive, so that he goes on learning and growing.
questions.rationale: “The state of doubt is a sort of intellectual shock… one needs a mind-set that admits that one does not know, not a mind-set that insists that one knows.”

questions.q: Animals act by instinct and are never “confused.” Why, according to the article, are human beings so often confused?
options: Human brains are weaker than animals’
Not quite. The article says: Man is free and must manage his own thoughts, sorting the relevant from the irrelevant in a flood of information.
Man is free and must manage his own thoughts, sorting the relevant from the irrelevant in a flood of information
Yes. This is the art of right thinking.
People have too little information
Not quite. The article says: Man is free and must manage his own thoughts, sorting the relevant from the irrelevant in a flood of information.
Confusion is taught in schools
Not quite. The article says: Man is free and must manage his own thoughts, sorting the relevant from the irrelevant in a flood of information.
questions.rationale: “Human beings have to manage their thoughts by themselves… They need to have the intellectual ability in order to discern the difference between what is relevant and what is not.”

questions.q: The article grants, for argument’s sake, that life developed by evolution. What does it say follows from that about belief in a Creator?
options: That there can be no Creator
Not quite. The article says: Nothing against it – a theory about the process of creation says nothing against the Creator.
Nothing against it – a theory about the process of creation says nothing against the Creator
Well reasoned. This is given as an example of sorting ideas correctly.
That science should be abandoned
Not quite. The article says: Nothing against it – a theory about the process of creation says nothing against the Creator.
That creation happened in six ordinary days
Not quite. The article says: Nothing against it – a theory about the process of creation says nothing against the Creator.
questions.rationale: “The theory of evolution is about the process of creation, not about the Creator Himself.”

questions.q: What does the article say the faultless harmony of so vast a universe shows?
options: That it has no laws at all
Not quite. The article says: That it is governed by a single all-powerful Controller.
That it is smaller than it seems
Not quite. The article says: That it is governed by a single all-powerful Controller.
That it is governed by a single all-powerful Controller
Correct. Otherwise it would fall into chaos.
That it is governed by many competing forces
Not quite. The article says: That it is governed by a single all-powerful Controller.
questions.rationale: “This perfect harmony in the universe can be understood as a proof that it is functioning under an all-powerful God.”

questions.q: People say “my house,” “my car,” “my property.” What does the article call these things?
options: Burdens best given away
Not quite. The article says: A “test-house,” a “test-car” – things lent for a time as a test.
Rewards for hard work
Not quite. The article says: A “test-house,” a “test-car” – things lent for a time as a test.
Signs of God’s special favour
Not quite. The article says: A “test-house,” a “test-car” – things lent for a time as a test.
A “test-house,” a “test-car” – things lent for a time as a test
Yes. At death they are all left behind.
questions.rationale: “In this world, every single thing is for the purpose of a test… the things he had thought of as his own had actually been given to him by God for a temporary period.”

questions.q: The Prophet prayed, “O God, give me guidance and show me the right way.” What does the second request add, in the article’s explanation?
options: Even on the straight path one needs to be kept from distractions that lead off into side lanes
Right. Guidance is needed continuously.
It repeats the first for emphasis
Not quite. The article says: Even on the straight path one needs to be kept from distractions that lead off into side lanes.
It asks for worldly success
Not quite. The article says: Even on the straight path one needs to be kept from distractions that lead off into side lanes.
It asks for a guide to travel with
Not quite. The article says: Even on the straight path one needs to be kept from distractions that lead off into side lanes.
questions.rationale: “Even after being guided to the straight path people have need of continuous guidance from God… ‘show me the right way’ means a request to be saved from distractions.”

questions.q: What does the article mean by “selective thinking,” of which Satan’s refusal is the first example?
options: Choosing one’s friends carefully
Not quite. The article says: Dwelling on the one thing one lacks while ignoring the many blessings one has.
Dwelling on the one thing one lacks while ignoring the many blessings one has
Yes. It leaves a person without gratitude.
Thinking only about useful subjects
Not quite. The article says: Dwelling on the one thing one lacks while ignoring the many blessings one has.
Remembering only happy events
Not quite. The article says: Dwelling on the one thing one lacks while ignoring the many blessings one has.
questions.rationale: “They ignore the good things that they do have and make a big issue out of the things that they do not have.”

questions.q: When a difficult situation arises, what course does the article recommend?
options: Not to react at once, but to stop and consider the likely results of one’s response
Exactly. Reaction sets off a chain of action and reaction.
To act first and think afterwards
Not quite. The article says: Not to react at once, but to stop and consider the likely results of one’s response.
To answer immediately and firmly
Not quite. The article says: Not to react at once, but to stop and consider the likely results of one’s response.
To leave the matter to others
Not quite. The article says: Not to react at once, but to stop and consider the likely results of one’s response.
questions.rationale: “The right course is not to take immediate action but to stop and reflect patiently on the possible consequences of one’s response.”

questions.q: A dying girl asked to be frozen in the hope of living again. What does the article say this longing for unending life points to?
options: That man’s nature seeks eternity, which is to be found not on earth but in Paradise
Well read. One must become a deserving candidate for it.
That the wish to live is a weakness
Not quite. The article says: That man’s nature seeks eternity, which is to be found not on earth but in Paradise.
That medicine will soon defeat death
Not quite. The article says: That man’s nature seeks eternity, which is to be found not on earth but in Paradise.
That the young fear death more than the old
Not quite. The article says: That man’s nature seeks eternity, which is to be found not on earth but in Paradise.
questions.rationale: “Eternal life is not possible on the planet earth. It requires a new world, that is, Paradise.”
